beats.text: You always think they started it. So do they.
Researchers had pairs of people press on each other's finger, with exactly the force they had just felt.
Nobody matched it. Each turn came back about thirty-eight percent harder.
Your brain dampens your own touch. So your push feels softer than theirs, even when it isn't.
And both sides were sure: I matched it. They pushed harder.
So in your next fight? You're probably hitting harder than you think.

sources: Shergill, Bays, Frith & Wolpert (2003). Two eyes for an eye: the neuroscience of force escalation. Science 301(5630):187. 6 pairs, tit-for-tat finger presses, 'a 38% mean escalation on each turn' over 8 turns; joystick condition matched accurately. Via Wolpert lab PDF + UCL press release.
